fields.h1: Build an App Feedback Survey That Points to the Next Fix
fields.hero_description: Build an app feedback survey that asks users about a screen right after they use it and keeps every answer in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into Your App Survey
fields.features_subheading: Describe your app and the moment to ask. Emergent builds the app feedback survey, and another prompt changes any part.
fields.feature_1:
Questions for each feature and screen

Name the feature or moment you want rated, such as a first bill split or day 3 of setup. Emergent writes the questions for it, and a follow-up prompt rewords any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Answers saved with screen and version

Each answer is saved as a row in a database you own, with the screen and app version you ask it to record. Filter by version to see what a single release changed for users.
fields.feature_3:
Bug reports sent to Slack or email

A problem report that crosses a rule you set, such as 5 reports naming one screen in 2 hours, sends a Slack or email alert. Single reports stay in the table until someone reads them.
fields.feature_4:
Short screens that suit a thumb

Phone users see one question per screen: a two-question survey takes two taps and an optional comment. The same survey opens in a desktop browser for people on the web app.
fields.feature_5:
Reports passed to your issue tracker

Send bug reports on to your issue tracker or help desk through its API. The engineer who picks up the ticket sees the screen and the user's own words, with nothing to copy over.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the source code

Run the survey on your own domain: custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository, next to the app's code.

fields.usecase_heading: App Feedback Surveys in Four Products
fields.tab_content_1:
44 users ask to split a bill by percentage

Pursewise shipped Split a bill and shows a short survey after each user's first split: how easy was it, from 1 to 5, and what got in the way? Over 21 days, 214 users answer and 61 rate it a 1 or 2. Of those 61, 44 ask in their comments to split by percentage instead of in equal shares.
fields.tab_content_2:
167 of 403 new runners stall on the watch step

On day 3, Stridewell asks each new runner one question per screen: what almost stopped you from logging your first run? Across 403 answers, 167 pick connecting a watch, well ahead of picking a plan at 98. The team moves watch pairing out of setup and onto the first run screen.
fields.tab_content_3:
Seven drivers hit one broken screen, and #driver-app hears

Haulbright Couriers puts Report a problem in its driver app menu. The form asks which screen the driver was on and what happened. When 5 reports name the same screen within 2 hours, the app posts in the #driver-app Slack channel. This morning, seven drivers report that the proof of delivery photo will not upload.
fields.tab_content_4:
Version 5.3 made search harder for 91 users

For a week after each release, Pennaway asks: did anything get harder in this update? A yes opens one more question, which screen. After version 5.2, 38 of 410 said yes. After 5.3, 126 of 388 did, and 91 of them named Search, where the filter bar had moved under a menu.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an App Feedback Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create an app feedback survey whose answers point to the next thing to fix in your app.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Keep it to two or three questions
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Save the context with each answer
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the one product decision the answers should settle, such as whether to add percentage splits or move watch pairing. Put it at the top of your prompt. Any question whose answer cannot change that decision comes out before launch.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask at a natural pause: after the first use of a feature, on day 3 of setup, or a week after a release. Never interrupt someone in the middle of a task, such as a checkout or a half-finished entry.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Lead with one closed question on a scale that stays the same between rounds, then one open question about what got in the way. Word each one the way users talk about the app, not the way your team names features.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List in the prompt what to save beside each answer: the screen and the app version, plus the device type if layouts differ by phone. A complaint about search can then be filtered and counted by release instead of read one by one.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set the alert rule for bug reports
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide how many reports on one screen, within how long, should alert someone, and who that person is. Start with a rule like 5 reports within 2 hours, then move the count once you know what a normal day looks like.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it on phones with five teammates
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the survey to five teammates and have them answer on their phones. Note any question they read twice and any answer choice they wish they had, then fix the wording with a follow-up prompt before launch.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the first week and act on it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read the first week of answers by screen and by version, then choose one change to ship. Mention it in the next release notes: that is how the users who answered learn their feedback was read.

faq_plan.q: What is an app feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: An app feedback survey is a short set of questions an app shows its own users about the app itself, such as a new feature or the latest update. Because each one is asked at a set moment in the app, every answer points to a screen or a release.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an app feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the app, the moment to ask, and the questions in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder. Emergent builds the survey and the database behind it. Link the survey from the screen where that moment happens, such as the confirmation after a first bill split, and change any part with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What are good app feedback survey questions to ask users?
faq_plan.a: Good app feedback survey questions are tied to one moment: How easy was this to do, from 1 to 5? What almost stopped you? Did this update make anything harder? Pair each scored question with a short open one that asks why, and drop any question your team will not act on.

faq_plan.q: Can an app feedback survey have a playful tone?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in one question at most. A light closing question, such as which animal the app would be, can make the survey feel less like a form. Keep the scored questions plain and worded the same every round, and save the joke for the last screen. A list of funny survey questions is a good place to borrow from.

faq_plan.q: When is the best time to show an app feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: Right after the user finishes something worth rating, such as placing an order or saving a first budget. Skip the first launch, when there is nothing to rate yet. Set a quiet period for each user, such as 30 days between surveys, which keeps the same people from being asked every week.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should an app feedback survey have?
faq_plan.a: Two or three for a survey shown inside the app: a scored question and an open one, plus an optional follow-up such as which screen. Save longer surveys for an email to users who opted in, and tell them up front how many questions it has.

faq_plan.q: Should an app feedback survey use a rating scale or a yes or no answer?
faq_plan.a: Use a scale to track a score over time and a yes or no answer for a single check. Ease from 1 to 5 after every release is a scale; whether anything got harder is a yes or no, one tap and easy to count. A yes no questions survey works well as a release check, with a comment box that opens only on yes.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more users to answer an in-app feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: Keep it short and say so: tell users up front that it is two questions, and put each question on its own screen. Give a busy user a clear skip button instead of a survey that blocks the app. A survey Emergent builds has no response caps, even in a launch week.

faq_plan.q: What should I do with the answers from an app feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: Give each answer an owner: bug reports go to the issue tracker with the user's own words, and feature requests go to whoever owns that part of the app. Reply to anyone who asked for help. With Emergent, every round lives in a database you own, and one release can be compared with the next before you choose what to fix.

faq_plan.q: Should an app feedback survey follow an in-app purchase?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once, on the screen that confirms the purchase, with one question about how easy buying was. Ask about the item itself later, after the user has had time to use it. That later question is the job of a post purchase survey, sent a few days after the order.

plan.angle: The searches behind this primary want the questions to ask app users and a way to run the survey; the AlsoAsked tree drifts to paid-survey apps, so the page stays strictly on teams surveying their own app's users. Question lists stop at the list. This page shows four app feedback surveys, each tied to one moment in the app and ending in a product decision: a budgeting app rating a new feature after first use, a running app asking new users on day 3 what nearly stopped setup, a courier's driver app whose problem reports post to Slack past a threshold, and a notes app asking after each release whether anything got harder. The FAQ covers questions, tone, timing, length, answer formats, response rates, what to do with answers and in-app purchases, as plain advice with no third-party claims.

findings.issue: The page follows the published sibling /ai-survey-and-quiz-builder/website-feedback-survey sentence by sentence with nouns swapped. Its tab 3: 'Oxbury Public Library puts a Report a problem link in the footer of every page. The form asks which page and what went wrong. When 3 reports name the same page within 24 hours, the app posts in the #web-fixes Slack channel. This morning, 4 reports...'. Also feature_3 'Single reports stay in the table until someone reads them' (sibling: 'Single reports wait in the table for review'); feature_4 'Phone users see one question per screen' (sibling: 'Visitors on a phone see one question per screen'); feature_6 'Run the survey on your own domain... On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository, next to the app's code' (sibling: '...and keep it with your site'); howto_step_1_des 'Put it at the top of your prompt. Any question whose answer cannot change that decision comes out before launch' (sibling: 'Write it at the top of your prompt. A question that cannot change that decision comes out before launch'); howto_step_5 alert-rule step mirrors sibling step 5. Same feature order and how-to arc. QC D2 passes (under 30% shared phrases) but the page reads as the website page with app nouns.
findings.fix: Next time: give tab 3 a different mechanism or story shape (e.g. a crash report with device and OS, or a ticket opened per report) and write step 1 and step 5 without the sibling's sentence frames.

findings.quote: Can an app feedback survey have a playful tone? ... A light closing question, such as which animal the app would be, can make the survey feel less like a form. ... A list of funny survey questions is a good place to borrow from.
findings.issue: HUB_RULES 5: every FAQ item must be a question a searcher of this keyword asks, never padded for a forced keyword or link. This item exists to carry the funny-survey-questions link and its advice ('which animal the app would be') sits oddly against the page's own rule of two or three questions that change a product decision.
findings.fix: Replace with a searcher question (e.g. whether to ask in the app or by email, or whether to make answers anonymous) and move the funny-survey-questions link or drop it.
